UN Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards (New York Convention, 1958)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), Articles L.561-1 et seq. and R.561-1 et seq.; UBO register provisions in Articles L.561-45 to L.561-51 C.mon.fin. and implementing decrees (Ordonnance n°2016-1635; Décret n°2016-1503), transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849 (4th AML Directive) as amended.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation / registered business certificate of each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Shareholder's corporate registry (e.g., State Administration for Market Regulation in China)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (where apostille convention in force) or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association / constitutional documents of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate shareholder's board of directors / notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / corporate existence certificate of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate registry or registered agent

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) natural person identification documents and ownership chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate shareholder and/or notary public

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of each shareholder, director, manager, and UBO against (i) French domestic financial prohibitions published by the Ministry of the Economy, (ii) EU consolidated financial sanctions list (European Council), (iii) United Nations Security Council sanctions lists, (iv) TRACFIN's typologies, and (v) for USD transactions, OFAC sanctions lists. Politically Exposed Persons are defined in Art. L.561-10 C.mon.fin.; enhanced due diligence must include source-of-funds analysis, two-year post-employment PEP caution period, and independent verification.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) and Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RNCS) accessible via Infogreffe
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be written in Latin script in the articles and registration file; non-Latin script must be transliterated into French/Latin characters. The name must be distinctive, lawful, and not contrary to French public policy. If a foreign-language word is used, the legal form indicator 'SARL' must appear in full French form. Misleading names or names suggesting a regulated activity or public authority are rejected.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not maintain a statutory priority name-reservation register; name clearance is verified at the time of incorporation filing through the Guichet unique/RNCS. In the event of a rejection based on a prior registered name or trademark, the applicant may (i) file an administrative request with the Directeur de greffe requesting reconsideration within 15 days, (ii) appeal to the Tribunal judiciaire (commercial chamber) within one month, or (iii) select a modified, distinctive name and submit a new incorporation file. Internal diligence search results may be held as a provisional reservation for 30 days only.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permitted — French law allows domiciliation through an approved commercial domiciliation company; however, the registered office must be a genuine address capable of receiving legal process and administrative correspondence. For a solar EPC contractor with physical construction sites, a purely virtual office raises a substantial risk of administrative recharacterization, tax residence challenge, and refusal of licenses. A physical project office or an operational base in the registered-economy location is strongly recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 0.40 (40% probability of an unannounced inspection within the first 36 months, especially if using a commercial domiciliation address or showing limited local substance)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal due diligence and AML/CFT screening of shareholders, directors, managers and UBOs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Paris flat fee for corporate KYC and SARL incorporation scope (range USD 700–1,200)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance search in RNCS/INPI and Infogreffe report
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registry search tariff plus fixed legal search fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalization / apostille of four foreign corporate documents (including sworn translation if required)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs / certified translation agency
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official apostille fee (approx. USD 20 per document) plus translation service (approx. USD 70 per page)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of articles of association (statuts) and in-house legal review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff schedule for capital-linked acts (scale B) or attorney flat fee for SARL incorporation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of mandatory legal announcement (avis de constitution) in a legal gazette (JAL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (e.g., Les Affiches Parisiennes)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Publisher's scale tariff per number of lines

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing of incorporation dossier and UBO declaration with the Greffe through Guichet unique
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fixed fee applicable to commercial registration and UBO declaration

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL provisions) and R.223-1 et seq.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (Articles of Association) and M0 form (Demande d'immatriculation)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum; capital is freely determined by shareholders, but must be fully subscribed and paid up for cash contributions. For non-cash contributions, a statutory auditor (commissaire aux apports) must be appointed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the shareholders subscribe to the shares of the company as set forth in the Articles of Association, and that all cash contributions be paid in full to the company's bank account. RESOLVED: That the registered office be established at the address stated in the Articles, and that the legal representative be authorized to file all incorporation documents. RESOLVED: That [Name] be appointed as Manager (Gérant) with full powers to act on behalf of the company, including opening bank accounts, signing contracts, and undertaking all actions necessary for the company's operation. RESOLVED: That the Manager is authorized to engage professional advisors and to take all steps required for regulatory compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Sign Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: All shareholders (and notary if real estate contributions are made)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the statuts in French, including company name, registered office, corporate purpose (solar farm EPC contracting), share capital, share distribution, management rules, and duration. All shareholders must sign the document. If contributions include real estate, notarization is mandatory.
required_dossiers: Shareholders' identification documents (passport or national ID)
Proof of residential address for each shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the statuts are incomplete or contain errors, correct and re-sign; if notarization is required, engage a notary to rectify.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal gazette (Journal d'Annonces Légales) authorized for the department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft a notice containing the company name, legal form (SARL), capital amount, registered office address, corporate purpose, and manager's name. Publish the notice in a legal gazette approved for the department where the registered office is located. Retain the publication certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notice is rejected due to formatting or content issues, correct and republish; ensure compliance with local gazette requirements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit Capital into a Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French bank or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary bank account in the company's name and deposit the cash contributions. Obtain a certificate of deposit (attestation de dépôt de fonds) from the bank, which is required for the incorporation filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deposit is insufficient or documentation is incomplete, request additional funds from shareholders or correct the bank forms.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Dossier with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed M0 form, signed statuts, proof of capital deposit, legal notice publication certificate, and other required documents. Pay the filing fee. The Greffe will review the dossier and issue a registration certificate upon approval.
required_dossiers: Proof of capital deposit (attestation de dépôt de fonds)
Identity documents of managers (passport or national ID)
Proof of registered office address (lease or ownership document)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the dossier is queried, the Greffe will issue a notice of incompleteness. Correct the deficiencies and resubmit within 15 days to avoid rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Registration Certificate (Extrait K-bis) and Tax Numbers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS) and French Tax Authority (DGFiP)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the company is registered and receives an extrait K-bis (official proof of incorporation). The SIREN/SIRET numbers are automatically assigned. The company must also obtain a VAT number (TVA intracommunautaire) from the tax authority.
required_dossiers: None (issued by registry and tax authority)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the K-bis is delayed, contact the Greffe directly. For VAT number, follow up with the local tax office (Service des Impôts des Entreprises).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: DREAL (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement) for environmental permits; Qualibat for professional qualification
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificat de qualification professionnelle (Qualibat) for solar installation

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DREAL (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full EIA Report (for utility-scale solar projects)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with French Environmental Code (Code de l'environnement) for wastewater, VOC emissions, and waste handling; adherence to ISO 14001 standards and local discharge limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (Commission de sécurité), structural load inspections (Bureau de contrôle), and workplace health and safety clearance (Inspection du travail).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP), Ministry of Economy and Finance; official tax portal: impots.gouv.fr; company formation and registration portal (Guichet Unique / INPI): formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a newly established French SARL: (1) file incorporation documents through the Guichet Unique operated by INPI, triggering automatic registration with the RCS (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés) and INSEE, which issues the 9-digit SIREN and SIRET establishment numbers; (2) the DGFIP Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) of the registered office allocates the intra-Community VAT number under Article 286 CGI, formatted as FR-AB-123456789, where AB is the two-digit control key and 123456789 is the SIREN; (3) file the taxpayer existence return (Imprimé M0), choose the VAT reporting regime (normal régime réel normal or simplified régime réel simplifié under Article 302 septies A CGI) and file the initial IS return (form 2065-SD); (4) for a non-resident company with French VAT nexus but no fixed establishment, direct registration with the DGFIP non-resident tax department (Direction des Non-Résidents / DRFIP) is required, and appointment of an accredited tax representative is mandated under Article 289 A CGI where taxable supplies in France exceed EUR 10,000 annually; (5) alternatively, non-established EU suppliers of distance sales or certain B2B services may report French VAT through the EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS/IOSS) schemes to obtain a French VAT reference without local registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — A French SARL is by default subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) on worldwide profits under Article 206-1 CGI. The standard headline IS rate is 25% (from 2022), with a reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,000 of taxable profit for eligible SMEs satisfying the Article 219-I-b CGI criteria (turnover below EUR 7.6 million and paid-in capital fully released, at least 75% held by individuals). No territorial scope privilege or tax-exempt zone status applies to a standard commercial SARL. Profits are reported on forms 2065-SD / 2058-SD with annual filing by the second business day following 1 May of each fiscal year; instalments are due 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France has no check-the-box or equivalent entity-classification election. Available statutory elections: (a) eligible family SARLs ('SARL de famille') may irrevocably elect income-tax pass-through treatment (régime des sociétés de personnes, Article 239 bis AA CGI) provided all associates are natural persons; (b) fiscal integration (régime de l'intégration fiscale, Article 223 A CGI) allows a 95%-or-more French parent to consolidate IS results of its French subsidiaries; (c) VAT filing-mode election between the normal and simplified regimes under Article 302 septies A CGI; (d) participation exemption on qualifying dividends under Articles 145 and 216 CGI with a 5% recapture; (e) hybrid mismatch alignment is statutory under Articles 209 and 212-1 bis CGI, with no elective hybrid-entity treatment; (f) arm's-length documentation and transfer-pricing election (Article L13 AA/LP) for controlled transactions. Renewable-energy EPC contractors should also consider the specific regime for long-term construction contracts covering more than 12 months under the IS realisation rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée — TVA), governed by Articles 256 to 289 D of the French General Tax Code (CGI) and Directive 2006/112/EC as transposed
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: French-established taxable persons must register for VAT as soon as taxable supplies commence; no economic turnover threshold applies for registration once operations are carried out. The small-business exemption (franchise en base de TVA, Article 293 B CGI) removes the obligation to charge VAT and to register until turnover exceeds EUR 91,900 for sales of goods and EUR 38,700 for services (2025 thresholds; intermediate thresholds of EUR 101,000 and EUR 47,700 trigger loss of exemption). Non-established foreign suppliers making taxable supplies in France have no exemption threshold and must register from the first euro of French taxable turnover; for EU sellers, distance sales of goods are reportable via the Union OSS scheme once cross-border turnover exceeds the EU-wide EUR 10,000 annual threshold. For an EPC contractor invoicing French VAT-liable clients, issuance of invoice with French VAT number and monthly or quarterly TVA returns (form 3310-CA3 or 3517-SD) is required.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory national e-invoicing and digital clearance (Article 289 bis CGI, Post-2026 French e-invoicing reform): all French-established businesses must receive structured electronic invoices, and phased issuance mandates apply — large and mid-size enterprises from 1 September 2026 and small/micro enterprises from 1 September 2027. Invoices must be issued in one of the authorised formats (Factur-X hybrid PDF/XML containing a 2D-Doc QR code and digital signature, UBL, CII or CEN-EN 16931 EDI) and routed through the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) operated by DGFIP or through an accredited partner platform (Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire, PDP). The PPF and PDPs perform real-time transmission and validation of invoice metadata and payment data, constituting an automatic fiscal-clearance mechanism that enables DGFIP to cross-check VAT returns, intra-community recapitulative statements and export flows. B2B invoices issued for solar EPC milestone payments must therefore bear the French VAT number of the purchaser and, where applicable, the reverse-charge or zero-rating mention; export invoices benefitting from Article 262-I CGI exemption must include a customs disposition in the invoice container and be transmitted with the underlying MRN via interconnectivity between the PPF and the national customs single window.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: export supplies of goods physically dispatched or transported from France to a destination outside the European Union are legally exempt from French VAT at the 0% rate under Article 262-I-1° CGI, provided the goods leave EU customs territory within 90 days of dispatch (extendable up to 14 months for specific construction or assembly sites outside the EU, which covers solar-farm equipment shipped to non-EU projects). The exporter must hold a valid customs export declaration (DAU / ENS) with a movement reference number (MRN). Services: contract work, processing, repair, maintenance and ancillary services (including engineering and installation work) directly relating to exported goods qualify for zero-rating under Article 262-II-3° CGI if the services are physically performed on goods destined for a third country; in addition, pure B2B engineering and consultancy services supplied to an overseas customer are outside French VAT where the place of supply is the customer's country of establishment under Article 259-1 CGI, and are therefore not chargeable with French VAT. For an EPC solar contractor, materials and components exported as part of a delivery order should be covered by one single export declaration; services performed at the overseas site are offshore supplies falling outside French VAT jurisdiction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU / ENS) with BAE/Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or CMR transport document evidencing physical cross-border movement
Commercial invoice issued to the non-EU buyer with the legal zero-rating reference (Article 262-I-1° CGI)
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT/MT103 credit advice demonstrating settlement of the export proceeds
Delivery note and site acceptance certificate (procès-verbal de réception) for EPC milestone or completed export
Supplementary transport documents (packing list, insurance certificate, EUR.1/CoO where preferential tariff claims are made)
Proof of on-site installation / commissioning report for solar EPC components exceeding the mere supply of goods where zero-rating of services is claimed
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFIP and customs authorities apply strict audit scrutiny to export zero-rating claims. Where documentation is incomplete, the tax authorities may requalify the supply as domestic and assess French VAT at 20% at the same time as debiting the exporter for input VAT that was deducted on the purchase of exported goods, producing a full reversal clawback plus interest. Penalties under Articles 1728 to 1730 CGI apply: late-filing assessment, 10% for negligence, 40% for deliberate inaccuracies, 80% for bad-faith (mauvaise foi) concealment, and 100% for fraudulent manipulation (manœuvres frauduleuses) of export evidence. Late-payment interest is charged at 0.2% per month (Article 1727 CGI), and an additional 5% audit surcharge applies for failure to respond to requests for information. In cases of customs export fraud (Code des douanes, Article 343-1 et seq.), seizure of the goods or their monetary equivalent and fines of up to twice the value of the undeclared goods may be imposed, together with prohibition from managing a business and criminal sanctions under Article 1741 CGI for tax fraud, including imprisonment up to five years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF) and the French Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority (ACPR) under the aegis of the European Central Bank (ECB) for monetary policy and foreign exchange operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a Eurozone member; the euro (EUR) is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. No exchange controls exist under EU law and the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier). Profit remittance is unrestricted, subject to standard corporate tax withholding (if applicable) and anti-money laundering (AML) verification. Dividends paid to non-resident shareholders are generally exempt from withholding tax under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, provided the parent holds at least 10% for 24 months. No prior authorization is required for capital movements, but statistical reporting to Banque de France is mandatory for cross-border transactions exceeding €12,500 per month.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion of export proceeds exists in France. Exporters may retain foreign currency in designated accounts or convert freely. However, all cross-border transactions must be reported to the Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistics, typically via the bank intermediary. The reporting threshold is €12,500 per transaction or cumulative monthly flows. No conversion ratio is imposed.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. France recognizes Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) under the EU PSD2 directive, regulated by ACPR. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., from UK or non-EU) may operate in France only under a passport or a French license. For a solar EPC contractor requiring project milestone wires and LC, a full-service commercial bank is preferable. EMIs often lack LC issuance capabilities and may have lower transaction limits. Legal constraints: EMIs cannot provide credit or hold client funds for extended periods; they are not suitable for escrow accounts. Viability is conditional on the EMI having a French or EU passport and robust correspondent banking network.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for the initial onboarding of a corporate entity. French banks mandate that at least one director or authorized signatory appear in person at a branch or via a notarized power of attorney. Remote opening is possible for EU-based directors using video identification (e.g., via ACPR-approved e-KYC), but for non-EU directors, physical presence or a visit to a French consulate is typically required. The bank will conduct a face-to-face interview to verify the business model, source of funds, and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction exposure (e.g., payments from or to sanctioned countries or tax havens)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a detailed transaction flow chart, underlying contracts (EPC agreements, invoices), and evidence of economic substance (office lease, payroll records). Obtain a legal opinion from a French counsel confirming compliance with EU sanctions and AML regulations. Include UBO declarations and proof of source of wealth for all shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual transaction patterns (e.g., large upfront payments from a single counterparty)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the full EPC contract with milestone schedule, bank guarantees, and performance bonds. Provide audited financial statements and a business plan. Explain the commercial rationale and provide third-party verification (e.g., credit insurance, independent engineering reports).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete UBO identification or complex ownership structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a corporate structure chart with all intermediate entities, certified copies of incorporation documents, and a legal opinion on the chain of control. Ensure all UBOs are identified with passport copies and proof of address. If any UBO is a PEP, provide a risk assessment and enhanced due diligence file.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sector-specific red flags (e.g., construction/EPC with potential for money laundering via over-invoicing)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide detailed cost breakdowns, third-party valuations, and independent cost certification. Include evidence of competitive bidding and adherence to industry standards. Maintain a robust internal audit trail and appoint a compliance officer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols: Use SWIFT MT103 for direct transfers. The purpose code must be 'G100' (Investment in equity capital) or 'G200' (Loans) under the French balance-of-payments classification. For capital injection, the bank will require a copy of the shareholders' resolution, the share subscription agreement, and proof of the source of funds. The transfer must be routed through a correspondent bank with a clear reference to the beneficiary's IBAN (FR76...). Verification includes anti-money laundering checks and confirmation that the sender is the actual investor. For loans, a loan agreement and interest rate documentation are required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: For project milestone payments to suppliers or subcontractors, use SWIFT MT103 for direct payments. For larger, structured transactions, a Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) is recommended. The LC can be issued by the French bank and advised through a confirming bank in the beneficiary's country. For EPC contracts, a standby LC (SBLC) may be used as a performance guarantee. All outbound payments must be reported to the Banque de France if they exceed €12,500. The bank will require supporting documents (invoices, contracts, customs declarations) to ensure compliance with trade sanctions and export controls.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/CNY, etc.) with a maturity up to 12 months, available from French banks without underlying transaction requirement (subject to credit line).

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible for exotic currencies (e.g., certain African or Asian currencies) where deliverable forwards are not available, but the EUR is fully convertible so NDFs are rarely used.
Cross-currency swaps (EUR vs. USD or other major currencies) for long-term hedging of project cash flows, subject to ISDA documentation and credit support annex.
Currency options (European style) for hedging uncertain future cash flows, available from major banks.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard rate; 15% reduced rate on the first €42,500 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs (turnover < €10 million, share capital fully paid, 75% owned by individuals or SMEs) plus 3% social contribution surcharge on taxable income exceeding €2.5 million
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday. Available incentives include the Research Tax Credit (CIR) at 30% of eligible R&D expenditure, optional accelerated depreciation for solar energy assets, and the Innovation Tax Credit (CII). Tax losses may be carried forward indefinitely with an annual utilization cap of €1 million plus 50% of taxable profit above €1 million (represented as zero finite-year limit); loss carryback for 3 years is available for certain SMEs.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form n° 2065-SD (Déclaration de Résultats) with supporting liasse fiscale (frames 2050-SD through 2059-SD), filed electronically via the impots.gouv.fr EDI/EFI professional portal; corporate income tax installments are remitted on Form n° 2571-SD
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with quarterly corporate income tax instalments)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the return must be filed by the second business day after 1 May (typically 3 May in 2024). For off-calendar fiscal year ends, the return is due within 30 days of the statutory deadline for shareholder approval of the annual accounts, which in all cases falls no later than 6 months from the fiscal year close.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SIREN, SIRET, legal form, French APE/NAF activity code, head-office address, fiscal year opening and closing dates, and mode of taxation (IS).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident enterprise operating through a permanent establishment, enter the French PE address and, if required, the joint fiscal representative's details. A shareholder or branch located abroad must provide parent-company identification within the declaration or an annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report construction and EPC contract turnover, project milestones, subcontractor costs, equipment purchases, direct labour expenses, and indirect operating expenditures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only French-source construction revenues attributable to the fixed place of business in France under Article 164 B CGI or the applicable DTA are reported; expense deductions must be directly connected to those revenues and evidenced by arm's-length invoicing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting result before tax adjustments, including banker's deposits, depreciation charges, and provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where the non-resident applies profit-attribution under a treaty, reconcile worldwide profit to the French PE result on a separate schedule; ensure inter-company service charges are eliminated or adjusted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses added back (e.g., excessive amortization, non-deductible interest, fines, donations) and deductible items such as Research Tax Credit offset, carryforward losses, and energy transition depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include transfer-pricing adjustments, French withholding tax credits, and only the allowable portion of inter-company payments to related foreign entities. Attach the Form 2065-SD transfer-pricing annex if the entity exceeds the €400 million documentation threshold.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable income after loss offset, application of the 15% or 25% corporate income tax rate, the 3% social contribution, and allocation of instalments already paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-residents, French-source income may also be subject to separate withholding taxes; tax credits for withheld amounts must be inserted here. The final balance or refund is computed after offsetting prior instalments and the 3% contribution if applicable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an automatic 10% late-filing surcharge on the tax due; the surcharge rises to 20% if the return is filed after formal notice, and 40% for intentional non-filing or abuse of law. In addition, monthly late-payment interest of 0.20% runs from the statutory due date. For zero-assessment filers, a flat fine of €1,500 may apply for failure to file within 30 days of the notice.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% statutory withholding tax under Article 187-1 CGI on dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders, reduced to 0% for qualifying EU corporate shareholders meeting the Parent-Subsidiary Directive conditions (minimum 5% shareholding held for 2 years) and further reduced under applicable double tax treaties for non-EU residents.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA reduction or exemption, the non-resident beneficial owner must submit a French tax-residence certificate (TRC) issued by the competent authority of the treaty state, together with a completed French claim application (Form 5000 series or relevant treaty-relief form) to the DGFiP or, for source relief at payment, to the paying company before distribution. The claim must be filed within the statutory period of four years from the withholding payment date and must include proof of beneficial ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: domestic statutory withholding tax of 33.33%; DTA rates commonly range from 0% to 20%. Interest on shareholder or intercompany loans: domestic rules generally impose 30% withholding on interest paid to non-treaty residents or in anti-abuse situations; under the EU Interest & Royalties Directive, qualifying EU recipients receive a 0% rate where a 25% direct or indirect shareholding exists, and treaty rates commonly reduce interest to 0%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Formal Local File and Master File are mandatory where the French entity (or the French permanent establishment) reports annual turnover or balance-sheet assets of at least €400 million. A Country-by-Country Report is additionally required where the group consolidates revenue above €750 million and the French entity is an ultimate parent, surrogate parent, or designated constituent entity. Below the €400 million threshold, documentation must still be prepared and produced in response to a DGFiP request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not have a separate ESR code, but applies the abuse-of-law doctrine (Article L64 LPF), EU ATAD anti-hybrid rules, limitation-of-benefits provisions in DTAs, and the DTA permanent-establishment requirement. A French SARL carrying on solar farm EPC contracting must demonstrate actual substance (real premises in France, employees with technical authority, operational management meetings, and commercial decision-making in France); an artificial shell or treaty-shopped structure will be recharacterized, denied treaty relief, and subjected to 80% penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and false corporate declarations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-declaration of EPC contract revenue, inflating construction costs using fictitious supplier invoices, concealing project income in foreign bank accounts, or creating shell entities to divert profits outside France.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment plus late-payment interest and a penalty of 80% of the unpaid tax for bad faith or fraudulent behavior; criminal conviction under Article 1741 CGI carries up to 5 years' imprisonment and a fine of €500,000 (or double the value of amounts evaded).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who knowingly participates in the false declaration is personally liable for tax fraud; the court may order civil restitution of the evaded tax, a travel ban, a management prohibition up to 10 years, and disqualification from public procurement contracts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer-pricing non-compliance and lack of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Entering into intercompany transactions (engineering services, equipment procurement, subcontractor margins) with related foreign entities at non-arm's-length prices, or failing to present the Master File/Local File when requested; creating a purely artificial French SARL without actual management, employees, or operational function to erode the tax base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment using the best available comparables; penalty of 5% on the reassessed amount of cross-border transfers when documentation is absent, plus a €15,000 fine per missing file; if abuse of law is established, an 80% penalty applies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If the artificial structure is found to be an abuse of DGFiP, directors may be jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt; repeat or fraudulent schemes trigger the criminal penalties of Article 1741 CGI, including imprisonment, management bans, and in serious cases a travel ban.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abuse of rights / shell company (abus de droit)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating or using a non-resident holding company with no real commercial function solely to avoid French corporate income tax or withholding tax on dividend and interest repatriation; exercising treaty shopping through an intermediary state without substantive business activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of Article L64 LPF results in recharacterization of the arrangement, an 80% penalty plus interest, and denial of treaty relief; where the violation triggers the concealment doctrine, a formal notice may lead to an additional 10% criminal surcharge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The courts can pierce the corporate veil: directors who are the effective authors of the abusive scheme may be personally assessed for the unpaid corporate taxes, subject to civil liability under company law, and may receive a French territorial travel ban and prohibition from managing a commercial company for up to 15 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using layering transactions — e.g., routing milestone payments through a chain of holding companies in different jurisdictions, redeploying fraud proceeds into real estate or treasury assets, or using crypto-assets to disguise the origin of profits derived from a fictitious EPC subcontract.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 324-1 of the French Criminal Code, money laundering is punishable by a term of 5 years' imprisonment and a fine of €375,000; aggravated offences involving an organized gang or abuse of professional functions carry 10 years' imprisonment and a fine of €750,000, with asset forfeiture orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be charged individually as principals or accomplices; the corporate veil will be ignored where the company is a mere instrument. Penalties include criminal fines, confiscation of assets, a travel ban, and an absolute prohibition on exercising any business activity in France.
